decided.subject: Operating facts inside award releases
decided.question: Award releases sometimes restate operating facts: Schneider WEF Lighthouse (El Paso on-time delivery 61% -> 97%, USD 43M backorders cleared amid data-center demand); Lenovo TIME/Fast Company (AI revenue 33-35% of group). Rule says awards yield nothing. Keep operating facts from award releases the way they are kept from financing releases?
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Award and ranking releases are treated like financing releases: the award, ranking, score and the awarding body's view yield nothing, but operating facts the company states about itself are kept. Added: Schneider El Paso (on-time delivery 61% to 97%, lead times -35%, $43M backorders cleared amid data-center demand; Beijing +30%) and Lenovo FY25/26 (revenue US$83.1B, AI-related revenue doubled to 33% of group). Lenovo's Q1 35% (Fast Company release) restates the Q1 FY2027 call, so no entry. ir_pull's headline filter stays as it is.

decided.subject: Edge labels vs new contract types
decided.question: Infineon -> Eaton edge is labelled 'power semiconductors for UPS' but the new contract is SiC for Eaton's MVSST solid-state transformer; Schneider's Equinix MV-switchgear pilot is a counterparty entry, not an edge. Widen the Infineon->Eaton label, and should named pilot deployments become edge contracts?
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): One edge per supplier -> customer pair: another product of the same relationship goes on the existing edge and the label is widened. Infineon -> Eaton (power_cooling.json) becomes 'power semiconductors for UPS and silicon carbide (SiC) power devices for medium-voltage solid-state transformers' via a new correction kind 'edge' (code diff below). A named pilot at a customer's live site is a deployment: Schneider -> Equinix with that pilot contract already exists (datacenter_construction_power.json), so that part is resolved. Lab demos stay demos.

decided.subject: Government subsidy amounts
decided.question: X-Fab Erfurt cleanroom release (10-05-2026) names EUR 127.4 million of EU Chips Act funding. Left out as financing-like. Should a public subsidy / grant amount for a capacity project be captured as a capex fact (keep), or stay out with financing terms?
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Captured. Grants, subsidies and incentives a company receives are company facts (Micron's CHIPS incentives were already on its node), unlike loans, offerings and credit lines. The X-Fab Erfurt entry (10-05-2026) now states EUR 127.4 million of EU Chips Act funding from the German federal government and the Free State of Thuringia, through a set correction on the existing entry. Rule bullet shared with question 88.

decided.subject: Equity-stake purchases and sales
decided.question: Verifiers deleted (a) Foxconn selling 5,544,000 Zhen Ding shares, an equity-method investee (gain NT$2.68B, 26.47% kept), MOPS 10-12-2026, and (b) Osaka Organic buying shares that made SANBO Chemical an equity-method affiliate, TDnet 10-09-2026, under the equity-investment exclusion. Keep ownership changes between supply-chain companies as company facts (no price), or keep excluding them?
decided.label: Foxconn MOPS material information: release 2317-20261012-1 (10-12-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Kept. An operating company buying or selling a stake that is or becomes a subsidiary, JV or equity-method affiliate is a structural fact, not financing; price, proceeds and gain stay out as deal terms. Re-added: Foxconn sold 5,544,000 Zhen Ding shares, 299,971,627 shares (26.47%) kept (MOPS 10-12-2026, no NT$ figures); Osaka Organic: SANBO CHEMICAL IND. became an equity-method affiliate after a Q3 share purchase (TDnet 10-09-2026; the alliance itself restates the H1 entry, so it is not repeated). Both labels need a new verifier pass.

The rules list litigation neither way.

decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Captured, matching what is already kept (Moderna patent suits, Rorze JPY 9,587M settlement, AstraZeneca's H1 disputes incl. the $220m Sheffield settlement). decided.subject: DoD Chinese Military Company designations
decided.question: Alibaba 6-K (06-09-2026): the DoD added Alibaba to its 1260H Chinese Military Companies list; captured with the company's own response (data kept safe). Baidu's 6-K the same day (same designation) was skipped. Capture such designations (then add Baidu next run) or remove Alibaba's entry?
decided.label: Alibaba 6-K (06-09-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Captured. A government listing that names the company (DoD 1260H Chinese Military Companies list, Entity List / export-control listings, sanctions) or its removal is a material company fact when the company's own filing or release discloses it, with the stated effect and the company's response attributed. Alibaba's 6-K entry stays; Baidu's 6-K (06-09-2026, 'Baidu Responds to Inclusion on U.S. CMC List') is added now from the saved file instead of waiting for the next run.

decided.subject: Strategic equity investments by partners
decided.question: Teradyne's $300 million strategic equity investment in FormFactor (8-K 10-13-2026, tied by Teradyne's CEO to the collaboration) was kept on FormFactor's node by the verifier, citing the NVIDIA -> Coherent / Marvell and MACOM -> IQE precedents. Keep such partner investments as relationship facts, or drop them as financing?
decided.label: FormFactor 8-K (10-13-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Kept - the verifier's call stands. An operating company's investment in a customer, supplier or partner that the filing ties to a commercial relationship (NVIDIA -> Coherent / Marvell, MACOM -> IQE, Teradyne -> FormFactor $300M) is a relationship fact: investor, amount and stake as stated plus the commercial tie; security terms (price per share, warrants, conversion, lock-up, registration rights) stay out, and the same money from a bank or fund is financing. No data change: FormFactor 8-K (10-13-2026) entry already holds it.

Both were left out as governance / financing. Record large strategic ownership changes or subsidiary IPO filings?
decided.label: VNET Group 6-K (09-21-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): VNET: recorded - a ~38.1% stake (650,424,192 Class A shares) bought by PJ Millennium I / II, whose GP is a Lochpine Capital subsidiary, an affiliate of CATL per the release, plus the investor-rights clause that VNET supports the buyers' computing-power-electricity coordination strategy and AIDC know-how (6-K 09-21-2026); no price. Westinghouse's confidential draft IPO registration is an offering: no map entry, one row for the section 10c financing log is provided. Rule bullet shared with question 57.

decided.subject: Licence and disposal values
decided.question: (1) In-licence upfront / milestone values (AstraZeneca H1 2026: Dizal $600m + up to $900m, CTTQ $200m + up to $1.9bn, CSPC $1.2bn + up to $3.5bn) were left out as deal price, while partner milestones (Daiichi Sankyo $25M / $100M) are captured - capture licence values? (2) Capacity SOLD (MW only, no proceeds; e.g. Brookfield Renewable Q2 2026: ~570 MW Europe, ~2,100 MW to Northview, 25% of 403 MW Maine hydro, Colombian 218 / 39 MW): the rules keep acquisitions' operating facts but say nothing on disposals - capture?
decided.label: AstraZeneca 6-K (07-27-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): (1) Captured: a licence is a contract, not an acquisition, so stated upfront, 'up to' milestones and royalties are kept like a supply contract's value (AZ-insitro $40M / $1.46B was already kept). Added from AZ's 6-K (07-27-2026): Dizal $600m + up to $900m, CTTQ $200m + up to $1.9bn, CSPC $1.2bn + up to $3.5bn. (2) Captured: disposals mirror acquisitions - what was sold, stake, buyer; never price, proceeds or gain. Added Brookfield Renewable's Q2 sales (~570 MW Europe, ~2,100 MW Northview, 25% of 403 MW hydro, Colombia 218 / 39 MW, 33% of 2.1 GW).

decided.subject: Bitcoin lending
decided.question: MARA 8-K (08-06-2026): '4,742 BTC loaned, ~$4.3M interest income' was removed by the verifier as treasury / financial-yield activity (the 2026-10-13 rule keeps a miner's production, holdings and sales; pledges are financing). Count lent BTC as holdings and keep it, or exclude?
decided.label: MARA Holdings 8-K (08-06-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Kept. Bitcoin a miner lends out is still its holdings (MARA reports the 4,742 loaned BTC inside its 35,577 BTC); lending is not the company raising money, so the 2026-10-13 financing exclusion does not reach it. The loaned BTC and the interest income the company reports from it are kept; BTC pledged as collateral and the facility it secures stay out. Re-added from MARA's 8-K (08-06-2026): 4,742 BTC loaned, ~$4.3 million interest income in Q2.

decided.subject: Government funding commitments
decided.question: The 10-18 nightly verifiers treated government funding the company RECEIVES as financing (skill section 2) and stripped it from tonight's first-call patches: Infleqtion and Rigetti U.S. Department of Commerce letters of intent (up to $100M each; Rigetti's for an equity stake), IBM's ~$1B CHIPS incentives for its quantum plan, Quantinuum's up-to-$100M CHIPS R&D letter of intent, D-Wave's ~$1.57M NSF award, Xanadu's Project OPTIMISM funding 'in final discussions', and Rigetti's NSF-funded PSC system note, AST SpaceMobile's J-LEO 'up to ~USD 1B non-dilutive government capital' (the Rakuten award itself kept), Unisys' 'partially funded by the U.K. government'. They also stripped cash balances that include equity / convertible proceeds (AST pro forma cash > $3.7B, Planet $865M, Rocket Lab ~$2.4B). Government agencies as PAYING customers of named contracts (DARPA Stage B revenue, Space Force / Navy / NASA contracts) were kept. Should grants, incentives and funding LOIs stay out as financing, or be captured as material facts on the company's node (the sources are saved, so they can be re-added)? And should cash balances that include raised money stay out too?
decided.label: IBM Q2 FY2026 (07-22-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-19 (user delegated): Grants, incentives, R&D awards and funding LOIs are company facts (amount, program, status, hedge); if the government takes equity the award stays, stake terms out; government loans stay financing (program kept). Cash balances, incl. pro forma, are kept without raise terms. Restored: Infleqtion / Rigetti DoC LOIs, Quantinuum CHIPS LOI, IBM $1B CHIPS incentives, D-Wave NSF ~$1.57M, AST J-LEO ~$1B, Unisys and Rigetti/PSC funding clauses, Xanadu CAD $195M (6-K); cash for AST, Planet, Rocket Lab, Infleqtion, Rigetti, Quantinuum, Xanadu.

decided.question: A filing names a government agency or research institution (U.S. Government, RIKEN) as a customer of a chain product (Quantinuum's quantum systems): relations/ row under the 2026-10-19 government-customer rule, or counterparty keys on the filer's node?

decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier): counterparty keys on the filer's node, no relations row. A customer of a chain product is a chain relationship, and a chain relationship never becomes a scope-'other' row; the 2026-10-19 government-customer rule covers products outside the chains (e.g. Primoris's state DOT highway work, Jacobs' PA Consulting public clients, which stay as rows). Applied: the two Quantinuum rows (U.S. Government, RIKEN) added tonight were removed before commit; the facts stay on Quantinuum's node.

decided.subject: DoD contract awards: counterparties and relations rows
decided.question: How are DoD award entries written when one paragraph names several awardees or a Space Systems Command activity under the Air Force heading, and do defense awards give relations rows?
decided.label: Northrop Grumman DoD contract award (10-05-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier): (1) a multi-award paragraph is written as 'one of N awardees on a $X ceiling', never as the company's own amount; (2) counterparty 'U.S. Space Force' whenever the contracting activity is Space Systems Command or another Space Force unit, even under the AIR FORCE heading ('U.S. Air Force' only for Air Force commands), the activity named in the signal; (3) defense awards for non-AI products (aircraft, munitions, radios, satellites, sustainment) give one relations row per company per agency (supplies, scope 'other', the agency as the award names it, citing the saved dod file); an award for a clearly-AI product stays on the node with counterparty keys. Applied tonight: (1) and (2) in the 79 DoD patches; (3) rows left for the next night (noted).

decided.subject: Foxconn Interconnect Technology
decided.question: FIT's 2025 annual report lists 'Customer B, a group of related companies (Note 34)' at USD 604,571 thousand; is that the filing naming Hon Hai Group (node Foxconn) by relationship, so a customer-share contract is due?
decided.label: Foxconn Interconnect Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-30-2026)
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier): yes. Note 34(a)(i) gives the identical total (Hon Hai 7,144 + subsidiaries 409,977 + associates 187,450 = 604,571; 2024 532,341), so the filing itself identifies Customer B by relationship (2026-10-06 rule, Airoha -> MediaTek precedent). Added FIT -> Foxconn in components/cpu_datacenter.json (FIT's general server-connector placement; nvda_b200 is generation-specific) with an 'annual report customer share' contract, no computed percentage. The connected-transaction caps stay relations/ rows (scope other).

decided.subject: Illustrative 'such as' relations rows (AST SpaceMobile, IonQ)
decided.question: relations/ast-spacemobile.json rows Google, American Tower, Bell Canada and relations/ionq.json rows Air Force Research Laboratory, DARPA, Oak Ridge National Laboratory quote only a 10-K 'such as' list (committed rows). Keep or remove?
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier): removed, a one-time fix like the 10-21 'relations committed rows' hand fix. The 10-19 rule says an illustrative 'such as' mention is not a row (Amazon -> Generate Biomedicines, Ineffable Intelligence precedents); the IonQ agencies are also customers of a chain product, which stay as counterparty keys (10-21 decision). The other AST rows each rest on their own agreement quote; Bell Canada keeps its row from the Q2 call ('key partners like ... Bell Canada'). check_relations will flag the removed committed rows once; they clear when tonight's publish commits the files.

decided.subject: Flexjet relations rows (Honeywell, Honeywell Aerospace)
decided.question: Two committed Flexjet rows carry words their cited files do not state ('term extended through 2035' on the Honeywell Aerospace 10-Q row; 'in the January 2026 settlement' on the Honeywell 10-K row). Edit them?
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier V3): one-time accuracy fix of the product text only (no relationship removed): the Aerospace 10-Q row drops 'term extended through 2035' (only the Honeywell 10-K states it), the Honeywell 10-K row drops 'in the January 2026 settlement' (the 10-K gives no date). check_relations flags the edited committed rows once; they clear when tonight's publish commits them.

decided.subject: Planet Labs launch-provider rows
decided.question: relations/planet-labs.json had 9 customer_of rows (ArianeGroup, Blue Origin, Firefly, ISAR, MHI, NewSpace India, Rocket Lab, SpaceX, Stoke Space) quoting only the 10-K sentence 'There are also a limited number of suppliers able to launch our satellites, including …'. Keep?
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier V3): removed. The sentence lists who is ABLE to launch, not who Planet buys from, so it states no relationship (illustrative-list rule, 10-19); the ArianeGroup row also mapped Arianespace to its parent from knowledge. Planet's stated launch partnerships keep their own rows (Isar Aerospace and SpaceX Transporter-18 from the Q2 FY2027 call). Committed rows: check_relations flags the removal once.

decided.subject: Platform-availability and duplicate relations rows (Xanadu, FIT)
decided.question: Rows added tonight: Xanadu customer_of Amazon / IBM ('PennyLane on public clouds …'), Xanadu partner Quantinuum ('organizations like Quantinuum'), FIT supplies Foxconn (framework sales cap, same relationship as the new FIT -> Foxconn customer-share edge).
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier V2): removed before commit. Platform availability is not a relations row (10-19 platform-integration rule); 'like Quantinuum' is an illustrative mention; an 'other' row may not repeat the relationship an AI edge already carries (§6). FIT's two customer_of rows (materials, logistics) stay.

decided.subject: Perplexity
decided.question: IREN's Co-CEO names Perplexity among IREN's new multiyear cloud contracts (Q4 FY2026 call); IREN and Perplexity share no chain file. Add a placement?
decided.label: IREN Q4 FY2026 (08-27-2026)

decided.subject: UMC customer sentence ('such as')
decided.question: UMC's 20-F: 'Our primary customers ... include premier integrated device manufacturers, such as Texas Instruments and Intel, plus leading fabless design companies, such as MediaTek, Realtek and Novatek.' Illustrative list or the company's own customer list?
decided.answer: Claude decision 2026-10-21 (independent Opus verifier V5): the company's own customer list. 'Such as' picks named members out of a set UMC itself calls its revenue customers, so the 10-05 / 10-19 customer-list rule applies, not the illustrative-example rule (which covers category examples never stated to be customers). The existing UMC -> Intel edge stands; a later run may add UMC -> MediaTek (foundry.json) and relations rows for Texas Instruments, Realtek, Novatek.
